text: The Event and Messaging Design v5 and the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog v1 are issued in Draft status with no approval recorded.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available, the run must not stop for one, and the overlay records the missing status as an assumption.
read: Both documents are complete and may be cited by the architecture, requirements and story documents of this run; the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of the architecture set.
applied_in: Read me sheet of both workbooks (status line)
impact: A document that a service story cites as the event contract carries Draft status until the approval is recorded.

text: TimerDue (EV-18) is read as retired: no TimerDue event type is provisioned, no topic carries it, and the timer is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow. TimerBreached (EV-19) stays the only timer event, published by rwb-case on rwb.case.events.v1.
why: The Ownership Map follows Architecture v5, which is first in R-PREC, and records EV-18 as retired with PLT as owner; the v4 row names the Case and workflow module. The two cannot both stand and the work package must choose one to write a topic catalogue.
read: The 30 entries of v4 remain 30 entries, of which 28 are event types on Kafka; EV-18 and EV-29 are not. No consumer subscribes to TimerDue and the rules component of v4 is reached inside the workflow instead.
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Events v5, row EV-18; catalog sheet Events and sheet Not on Kafka
impact: If TimerDue is kept as an event, a rwb.case topic event and a consumer in rwb-decision return, and the timer check job JOB-05 changes shape.

text: PartnerResultSubmitted (EV-21) is read as published by rwb-partner (S9) on rwb.partner.events.v1, with rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case as consumers; the partner portal is the external channel into rwb-partner and not the owner of the event type.
why: Architecture v5 slide 43 row 21 is first in R-PREC and gives producer, topic and consumers; the Ownership Map records S9 as owner with the same reading. Only the v4 direction and owning module disagree.
read: The event still enters the Workbench from outside through the partner gateway; what changes is that rwb-partner receives the result and republishes it on its own topic, so no service subscribes to an external system directly.
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Events v5, row EV-21; catalog sheet Events, sheet Topics and sheet ACLs
impact: If the event stays consumed from outside, rwb-partner loses a published type and three consumers need a direct external subscription.

text: AceDataReady (EV-26) is read as published by rwb-source-data (P1) on rwb.source-data.events.v1 after it reads recovery.v_ace_batch_status, with rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation and rwb-writeoff as consumers; the exemption from the Transactions rule is kept because the event is raised from the ACE batch record and not from a Workbench change.
why: Architecture v5 slide 43 row 26 is first in R-PREC and gives producer, topic and consumers; ACE ingestion is outside the 19 services, so no target service can consume the event from it; the Ownership Map records P1 as owner.
read: The payload keeps the source column names of the view: sourceSystem (source_system), businessDate (business_date), status and completedAt (completed_at).
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Events v5, row EV-26 and sheet Rules v5 additions, row Transactions; catalog sheet Events
impact: If the exemption is dropped, an outbox row would be required for a read that changes nothing in rwb_source_data.

text: Each of the 20 event topics has three retry topics, one per window of 1 min, 10 min and 1 h, giving 60 retry topics in the set. Their names are not stated by any source and are left to the platform story RWB-PLT-N002-INF, so this catalogue records the count, the window and the owner of each retry topic and no name.
why: Architecture v5 slide 9 fixes the three windows and RWB-PLT-N002-INF fixes the count of three per event topic; neither gives a name, and a name written here would be invented and would collide with the platform catalogue.
read: A retry topic carries one retry window and the same partition count as its event topic; a record walks the three windows in order before the dead-letter topic. A service story binds to the retry topics only through the library, never by name.
applied_in: Catalog sheet Retry topics; sheet Read me (topic count 100)
impact: Until the naming rule is agreed, no service can bind to a retry topic by name and the replay runbook cannot name one.

text: Each dead-letter topic is named by the suffix the source gives: the event topic name followed by .dlt (for example rwb.case.events.v1.dlt). It carries the same partition count as its event topic, one alert per record and a replay tool; its replication factor and retention are left to the platform story.
why: Architecture v5 slides 9 and 22 say a failed record goes to '.dlt' and RWB-PLT-N002-INF says one dead-letter topic per event topic with the same partition count; a name can be derived from the suffix the source states, but its replication and retention cannot.
read: Twenty dead-letter topics exist, one per event topic, including one for rwb.decision-record.v1. The name is derived and is confirmed with the platform story before the first apply.
applied_in: Catalog sheet Dead-letter topics; sheet Read me (topic count 100)
impact: If the platform uses a different dead-letter naming rule, 20 names in the catalogue and in every alert route change.

text: The shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 takes the same settings as the service topics: 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, cleanup policy delete and key caseId.
why: Architecture v5 gives settings for the service topics only; the shared topic carries the same kind of business fact and RWB-PLT-N002-INF already reads it that way, so one reading is applied rather than 19 different ones.
read: A rebuild of the central ledger can replay 7 days of the shared topic; the ledger remains the record and the topic is transport.
applied_in: Catalog sheet Topics, row rwb.decision-record.v1; Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Topics, same row
impact: A different retention on the shared topic shortens or lengthens the replay window of the central ledger and the reporting read model.

text: The v4 failure rule is read in the target as: a consumer failure is retried on the three retry topics and then the record goes to the dead-letter topic of the producing service, with an alert and the replay tool as the recovery path; the 'exception queue' of v4 is the dead-letter topic and the owner named by the rule is the producing service.
why: Architecture v5 slides 9 and 22 replace the in-process queue with the retry ladder and the dead-letter topic; no source keeps an exception queue in the target.
read: No exception queue table is provisioned and no screen is built for one; the alert route and the replay tool own the failure path.
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Rules v5 additions, row Failure; catalog sheet Delivery rules
impact: If an exception queue is kept, a new table, a screen and a manual drain step return to every service story.

text: The payload of the 15 event types named only in the Architecture v5 service catalogue is left to the CON story of the owning service and to the registry; this catalogue names the type, the topic and the owner and writes the payload placeholder of Template and Rules R9.
why: No source gives a field list for these types and a field list written here would be invented; the producing service owns the schema under the same rules as the 28 types v4 states.
read: The 15 types are ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished, FileDelivered, FileFailed, RouteDecided, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled, LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, AssetSold, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged. Each is a fact already implied by its name and topic, and each needs a schema before its first consumer is built.
applied_in: Catalog sheet Events, payload column of the 15 rows
impact: Fifteen of 43 event types have no registered schema yet; a consumer of one of them cannot be built to contract.

text: The consumers of ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished and LawsuitFiled are left open, and no read ACL is granted for them until the consumer list is confirmed; the catalogue records the gap in place of a consumer.
why: Slides 42 and 43 give a consumer list for every event they carry, and these three types are not carried there; a consumer written here would be invented and would widen an ACL.
read: The three types can be produced from the first release of their service; no service may subscribe until the list is confirmed.
applied_in: Catalog sheet Events (consumers column) and sheet ACLs (read list note)
impact: Three event types have no reader in the first release; rwb-reporting and gateway-bff are the likely consumers and are not assumed.

text: No registry subject is named in this version. The catalogue names the event type, the topic and the payload field list, and the subject naming rule is left to the registry story RWB-PLT-N008-INF and to the CON story of each producing service.
why: Architecture v5 requires a JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility but names no subject; a subject written here would be invented and could not be registered.
read: Compatibility is BACKWARD as Architecture v5 states; a consumer accepts the current and the previous schema version, as the v4 Versioning rule states.
applied_in: Catalog sheet Topics (schema column) and sheet Delivery rules
impact: No producer can register a schema until the subject rule exists; the event type names in this catalogue are ready to become subjects.

text: The envelope records the CloudEvents binary-mode headers ce_id, ce_type, ce_source and ce_subject, the W3C traceparent header and the record key caseId; the value forms of ce_source and ce_subject are left to the event naming library RWB-PLT-E1047-CON.
why: Architecture v5 names the four headers and the trace header but gives no value form for ce_source and ce_subject; ce_type follows the naming rule rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1 and ce_id is the event identity that the inbox stores.
read: A consumer routes on ce_type and dedupes on ce_id; it never routes on ce_source.
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Envelope; catalog sheet Envelope
impact: If the library chooses another form, the routing rules of every consumer are unaffected and only the header values change.

text: The idempotency key of an event is its ce_id, the inbox table processed_event holds ce_id as its key, and the duplicate count of R-UNI-40 is taken from that table.
why: Architecture v5 slide 22 states that each consumer records ce_id in its inbox in the same transaction as its own change, which is the only key the target stores; the v4 rule requires a key but does not derive a second one.
read: A redelivered event finds its ce_id in the inbox and is ignored; one count per service is kept for the rule report.
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Outbox and inbox; catalog sheet Outbox and inbox and sheet Delivery rules
impact: If a separate key is chosen, every producer and consumer carries a second identifier that no source defines.

text: Every event type is named rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1 as Template and Rules R4 requires, where short is the service that owns the type; DecisionRecorded is therefore rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 on the shared topic, and the 15 types that exist only in the Architecture v5 catalogue carry no EV number, so no number is invented for them.
why: The v4 table numbers EV-01 to EV-30 and gives no event type name; R4 fixes the name pattern and the Ownership Map fixes the owner of each type, so the name can be derived from two sources without inventing a value. A new EV-31 to EV-45 sequence would collide with any future version of the catalogue that numbers its own rows.
read: The 28 types that have an EV row keep that row and gain a type name; EV-18 and EV-29 have no type name because they are not topic events; the 15 catalogue-only types are keyed by name.
applied_in: Event and Messaging Design v5, sheet Events v5; catalog sheet Events, column Event type
impact: If a future version numbers the 15 types, the register gains EV-31 to EV-45 and the names are unchanged.
